transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is this... constant restless feeling. It’s like I’m just wound too tight and I can’t fully settle down. Even when I’m supposed to be doing something calm, you know? Like sitting through a planning meeting at work—I’m a retail buyer, and our seasonal forecasting meetings are just endlessly long. Actually, last week, my manager brought in these scones from that new bakery on 4th street, the one with the green awning? They were so incredibly dry, I couldn't even finish half of one, and they didn't even bring butter. 

But anyway, I just can't settle during those meetings. Or even when I'm trying to do something relaxing on my own time, like painting, or doing yoga. I started this new Vinyasa class on Tuesdays, and the instructor plays this really strange ambient flute music that just echoes off the studio walls and... wait, what was I saying? Right, the restlessness. I just always feel wound up, even when I'm supposed to be completely still.

When you feel this wound-up, restless feeling, is your mind also racing with worries or concerns? Or is it more that your body just feels like it needs to move, even if your mind isn't particularly anxious?

No, I wouldn't say I'm worried about anything. It's not like an anxious thing where I'm stressing over, I don't know, paying bills or something. It's definitely more of a physical thing. Like my body just has all this pent-up energy and needs to do something, so my foot will just start tapping on its own. 

I mean, my thoughts do jump around a lot, but it's not worry. It's more like... I'll be sitting there and suddenly remember I need to call our vendor about the summer linen order. We're doing this huge push on breathable fabrics this year because last summer was just so incredibly hot. I remember my air conditioning went out in July and it took the repair guy three days to come out. Three days! And he charged an absolute fortune just to replace this tiny little fuse that I probably could have bought at the hardware store for two dollars if I'd known what to look for. The guy's name was Jerry, I think, and he kept tracking mud onto my hallway runner... 

But, um, anyway. No, it's not anxiety or worrying. It's really just my body feeling like I need to get up and walk around or do something with my hands.
How long have you been experiencing this restless, wound-up feeling with the racing thoughts and the need to move around? Has this been going on your whole life, or did it start more recently?

Well, I guess I've always been a bit high-energy, but it really became noticeably harder to manage... let's see, it's been about two years and two months now. Right around the time when the conflicts with my in-laws started taking over, well, basically all of our evenings. 

My mother-in-law, she just has this way of making these little comments, you know? Like she’ll come over and point out that the throw pillows on the couch don’t match the rug. And I’m like, 'Susan, they’re supposed to be complementary, not identical.' I spent three weeks sourcing those pillows from a boutique in Santa Fe. They have this gorgeous hand-woven geometric pattern—the artisan actually uses natural dyes made from local plants. It’s fascinating, really, the whole process of extracting the color from the roots and leaves. I watched this whole documentary about it on a Sunday afternoon when my husband was watching football. He always watches the games with the volume turned up way too loud. I keep telling him it's going to ruin his hearing, and then he'll be one of those older men who just nods and smiles at dinner parties because he can't hear a word anyone is saying... 

But, right, the timeline. Yeah, it's been about two years and two months since it got really hard to just sit still and deal with it all.
When you were in school—elementary, middle, or high school—did your teachers ever comment that you had trouble paying attention, or that you were fidgety or talked too much in class?

Oh, definitely. Yeah, my mom kept a whole file of those notes from my elementary school teachers. I was always getting in trouble because I'd just pop right out of my seat during quiet time, or I'd be talking over the other kids. And I was terrible about blurting out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question. I just felt like I already knew where they were going with it, so why wait, right? 

It actually reminds me of this one time in fourth grade, Mrs. Gable's class. She had this huge terrarium in the back of the room with a bearded dragon named Spike. We were supposed to be doing a math worksheet, but I was so fixated on watching Spike eat these crickets. Did you know they can eat, like, dozens of crickets in a week? My nephew just got a reptile, actually, a leopard gecko, and my sister is absolutely terrified of the live food. She makes her husband use these long tweezers to drop the mealworms in. I told her she should have just gotten him a hamster, but apparently hamsters are nocturnal and keep you up all night running on that squeaky little wheel. I had a hamster named Barnaby when I was eight, and my dad ended up having to oil the wheel with WD-40 at two in the morning because nobody could sleep... 

But anyway, yeah, the teachers definitely noticed. Lots of notes home about the talking and not staying in my seat.
